newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end sharply lower after Iraq attack.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end sharply lower after Iraq attack.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended sharply lower on Tuesday after the U.S. launched cruise missile strikes against targets in Iraq, adding more negative sentiment to a market already suffering from interest rate woes.

The Hang Seng index ended 149.39 points lower at 10,957.18. Turnover was HK$4.16 billion, boosted by a burst of selling at the start of the afternoon session as investors reacted to news of the Iraq attack. Turnover on Monday was HK$2.85 billion.
"It definitely came as a surprise. I don't think people were really looking at this in an awful lot of detail," said Alan Hutcheson, director of research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
They said they were cautiously waiting for Wall Street's return from Monday's Labour Day holiday later.
The U.S. August National Association of Purchasing Management index, to be released on Tuesday, should give more clues about interest rates, they said.

"The fear of interest rate hikes and now a repeat of the Gulf War may dampen sentiment further in the short term. A technical correction is inevitable and we expect the downside will be at 10,800 (points)," said Edward Chan, research director at Standard Chartered Securities.
Interest rate sensitive banks took a hit. HSBC ended HK$2.50 lower at HK$129.50 and Hang Seng Bank fell HK$0.75 to HK$78.50.

H-shares tumbled 19.37 points to 775.39 with Zhenhai Refining off HK$0.20 to HK$2.075 on fears the U.S. attack will trigger higher oil prices. Shanghai Industrial fell HK$0.45 to HK$13.55 after posting first half net of HK$73.26 million versus proforma combined net of HK$186.66 million.

China Motor Bus rose HK$0.50 to HK$78.00 after Swire said it will start pre-sales of Island Place - jointly owned by Swire and China Motor Bus - at an average HK$6,282/sq ft next week. Swire fell HK$0.75 to HK$68.00. --J. Genevieve (852) 2843 6345
